examples.title: See the repeated order totals
Sum the expanded result
examples.sql:
SELECT sum(o.order_total) AS revenue
FROM orders o JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id;

examples.title: Aggregate items before joining
examples.sql:
WITH item_totals AS (
  SELECT order_id, count(*) AS item_count, sum(line_total) AS item_total
  FROM items GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.id, o.customer, o.order_total, i.item_count, i.item_total
FROM orders o LEFT JOIN item_totals i ON i.order_id = o.id
ORDER BY o.id;

examples.title: Count each order once
examples.sql: SELECT sum(order_total) AS revenue FROM orders;

sampleSpecs.title: Orders: one row per purchase
sampleSpecs.description: The three order totals add up to 240. Amounts are whole currency units in this fictional example.

sampleSpecs.title: Items: several rows per purchase
sampleSpecs.description: An order total belongs to the order. A line total belongs to one item row.

challenge.title: Total the orders with at least two items
challenge.prompt: Return one column, revenue, summing order_total once for each order that has at least two item rows.
challenge.hint: Find qualifying order IDs first, then filter orders with IN or EXISTS. Do not sum the expanded item join.
challenge.success: Ada and Cy qualify. Their order totals contribute once each: 180.
